title: Video of a game to a Game Code
author: LeanEntropy
selftext:
So, 3 weeks ago I showed a few friends and a small AI Game Dev community I'm in that I developed a tool + workflow to turn a video of a gameplay, both 2D and 3D, into actual game code - using Claude Code and a game engine (Godot in this case).  
  
My workflow managed to create the game code for Smash Fest from about 8 minutes (total) of video, in about 1 night + early morning of working independently. This includes the level design of the levels and all the meta game screens that appeared in the videos, plus the foundation that allowed me to generate new levels as well.  
  
I did not try to recreate the art and textures (copyrighted, a waste of time and tokens), just the code and made sure the scenes are built correctly so I could change asset for asset. The result was a working game.  
  
Since I've seen people found this interesting, I decided to share an overview of my process in this post:  [https://civax.net/posts/from-a-phone-video-to-working-game-code](https://civax.net/posts/from-a-phone-video-to-working-game-code)

Feel free to ask questions or to tell me my workflow suck and share your way better one...
